correctness.rationale: The canonical cut projector is B (B^T B)^{-1} B^T for the grounded incidence matrix of the unit fan K_1 join P_n. Re-derive the inverse Green kernel G_ij=F_(2 min(i,j)-1)F_(2(n-max(i,j))+1)/F_(2n) by the continuant and endpoint conditions. For a spoke source, the potential is positive and single-peaked, so the spoke currents sum to one and path current variations telescope; for a path-edge source the Green difference has opposite signs on the two sides. This yields separately the four absolute-column formulas (1)-(2) in RESULT.md. Their Fibonacci differences locate the maxima centrally; the explicit central path-vs-spoke comparisons are strictly positive except n=3 cut ties. Thus Q and I-Q exchange 2-2/L_n and 2-1/F_n with n parity; n=2 gives Q=4/3,C=1, n=3 both 3/2. As real symmetric operators their l1 and linfinity norms equal. Auditor-written exact rational incidence inversions separately reproduced every whole-column absolute sum and maximizer for n=2..9, including (-1)^n(Q-C)=F_(n-3)/F_(2n), not a proof beyond n=9.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns the sharp l1/linfinity absolute edge-current totals of the two canonical orthogonal projectors on fan graphs, not optimal projection constants over all projectors or ordinary pairwise resistance. Full HTML of Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii addresses invariant/minimal cycle-space projections for tori and Hamming graphs. The independent full-text reading of Sedlak–Slavik concerns fan Green entries, effective resistance and Kirchhoff indices, not maximal absolute current columns; this prior Green kernel is explicitly credited. The precise central edge-class and Fibonacci–Lucas parity interchange survived the inspected comparisons, with possible unindexed electrical-current formulations retained as risk.

value.rationale: A family-wide exact classification of two complementary, canonical edge-space projectors displays alternating dominance, an exponentially small exact gap, and distinct unique central maximizing edge classes on a natural triangular graph family. This requires absolute electrical-current and global extremizer analysis beyond the known Green kernel and is independently useful in graph Hodge/transport geometry.

limitations: Only unweighted finite fans and their Euclidean orthogonal cut/cycle projectors; not arbitrary projection constants.
